Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 110, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Nasr

It is a Madani surah.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿When the help of Allah comes and the victory﴾. They are unanimous that al-Fath (the victory) is the conquest of Makkah. It has been said that al-Nasr (the help) is also in it, and it is said that al-Nasr is the Day of al-Hudaybiyah. The first view is the most apparent and the most well-known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 110, verse 2:

And His saying: ﴿And you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes﴾. That is: in companies, company after company, and group after group.

In the tafsir (exegesis) it is related that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, the polytheists said: "Muhammad has been given victory by Allah over Quraysh, and they are the people of Allah and the people of His sanctuary. Allah had repelled the elephant from them, so no hand (yad) can be raised against Muhammad," meaning: there is no strength. So they entered his religion in multitudes, and whole tribes would embrace Islam together. Delegations (wufud) came to him from every direction, and most of the regions of the Arabs entered Islam, and only a few remained outside it. Before that, one or two would enter it in great fear. This is the meaning of His Exalted saying: ﴿And you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 110, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, that is: pray while praising your Lord.

The more correct view is that its meaning is: mention Him with praise and thanks for this great blessing, for tasbih (glorification, i.e. remembrance of God) has the sense of dhikr (remembrance). Thus the meaning of the verse becomes: remember your Lord with praise and thanks.

And His saying: ﴿and seek His forgiveness﴾, that is: ask for His pardon and forgiveness.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾, that is: Accepting of repentance from His servants. It is said: al-Tawwab is the one who facilitates the path of repentance; and it is said: He is the one who accepts it.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that in this surah there is an announcement of the Prophet's own death, and that he was commanded to glorify and seek forgiveness so that the end of his affair and the conclusion of his deeds would be increased obedience and remembrance of God.

It is also reported that 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to gather the Muhajirun and consult them on a matter, and he would bring Abdullah ibn 'Abbas along with them. They said: "O Commander of the Faithful, we have sons like him, yet you do not bring them." He said: "He is from where you know." Then he once asked them about this surah, and they said: "Allah the Exalted commanded the Messenger of Allah to glorify and seek forgiveness when victory came and people entered the religion in multitudes." He then asked Abdullah ibn 'Abbas about the meaning of the surah, and he said: "O Commander of the Faithful, Allah the Exalted announced to the Messenger of Allah his own death through this surah, and commanded him to increase in deeds and remembrance, so that it would be the conclusion of his life." Thereupon 'Umar said to the rest of the Muhajirun: "I bring him only for this and similar things," or words to this effect. The wording mentioned in the Sahih regarding this report is that Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is only the term of the Messenger of Allah which he informed him of," and 'Umar said to him: "By Allah, I know nothing of it except what you know."

It is said: the surah was revealed in the middle of the days of Tashriq.

It is said: the Messenger of Allah did not live after this surah except for eighty nights.

It has been said: it is the last complete surah to be revealed of the Qur'an, and Allah knows best.
